newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton dips on rains in producing regions.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton dips on rains in producing regions.

text.p: Cotton prices lost recent gains on the local market on Monday, dealers said.
Reports of fresh rains in the producing centres prompted unloading by stockist and state-owned agencies, dealers said.
"Cotton prices remained firm last week due to dry spell in the producing centres but now rain is here again and prices are coming down," one broker said.
There was little fresh mill demand at the improved level.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi slid by 5/10 rupees to 1,000/1,075 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned fell by 20 rupees at 1,825/1,860 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan moved down by 100/300 rupees at 14,200/14,700 rupees per candy (355.56 kg) while wagad cotton was steady at 13,200 rupees so was Kala-ginned at 12,500 rupees per candy.
